chapters.title: Skills and entitlements
chapters.subtitle: Who can help, and where they may work

steps.text: Skills describe what an agent can do, and entitlements decide where an agent may work. This video shows why they exist, how to create a skill, and how to give an agent queues, campaigns and skills.

chapters.title: Why skills and entitlements
chapters.subtitle: The right agent for every customer

steps.text: Not every agent can help every customer. A customer who speaks Spanish needs an agent who speaks Spanish, and a billing question needs someone who knows billing.
A skill describes what an agent can do, such as Spanish, Billing, or Tier 2 support. A queue can require or prefer skills.
An entitlement record decides which queues and campaigns one agent may sign in to, in what order the agent is offered work, and which skills the agent holds.
Skills are created once, in a list. They come with the work distribution feature of the Contact Center.
Each agent has one entitlement record: allowed queues with a priority and a delay, allowed campaigns, and skills with a proficiency from one to five.
Entitlements are a feature you turn on. Without it, any agent may sign in to any queue or campaign, and there is no screen to give agents skills.

chapters.title: Create a skill
chapters.subtitle: A name for what agents can do

steps.text: Open Interaction Center, Management, Skills. The list shows the skills that exist. Click Add Skill.
Enter a Name, such as Tier 2 support, and an optional Description.
Leave Enabled ticked and click Save. A disabled skill stays on the agents and queues that already use it, but it cannot be picked for new ones.
Open Agent entitlements, and click Add agent entitlements.
Click Browse users, search for the person, and pick them as the User. Each user has one entitlement record, and the screen tells you if one already exists.
Under Allowed queues, pick every queue the agent may sign in to. Removing a queue later also signs the agent out of it.
Queue preferences list the allowed queues. A lower Priority number is served first. Delay makes a caller wait that many seconds before this agent is offered work, so the agent can back up a queue.
Under Allowed campaigns, pick the dialer campaigns the agent may work. This site has none yet.
Under Skills, click Add skill, and pick a skill.
Set its Proficiency from 1, basic, to 5, expert. A queue that requires a skill at a minimum proficiency only offers its work to agents at or above it.
Click Save. The agent can now sign in to these queues, and receives work that matches their skills.
The list shows how many queues and campaigns each agent is allowed. Edit changes a record. Entitlement records cannot be deleted: remove the queues and campaigns instead.
Supervisors need a record too. The Live dashboard and the shared voicemail show a supervisor only the queues and campaigns on their own record, so without one their dashboard is empty.
A Spanish queue that only offers work to agents with the Spanish skill.
A backup agent, with a delay on the sales queue, who helps only when the sales team is busy.
A senior agent with Tier 2 support at proficiency 5, for the hardest questions.
A supervisor with a record for the queues they supervise, so the dashboard shows their team.
Create the skills, give every agent an entitlement record, and work reaches the people who can help. Thanks for watching.
